newsitem.title: UK: Dollars dominate Eurobonds with Toyota, Kellogg.
newsitem.headline: Dollars dominate Eurobonds with Toyota, Kellogg.

text.p: Continuing the pattern seen in recent weeks, the Eurobond market saw further jumbo dollar bonds launched on Tuesday.

Triple-A rated car manufacturer Toyota Motor Corp issued a $1.0 billion five-year bond in Asia, which will be priced later to yield 10 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. CSFB and Merrill Lynch were joint lead managers.
U.S. food maker Kellogg Co launched a $500 million four-year bond. Rated AA1/AA, the deal was priced at seven b.p. over three-year Treasuries, or around flat to the curve.
Bankers said although the pricing of the Toyota deal was fair, sales were subdued.
"The market is very high and U.S. yields are too low, and added to that the five-year market is very well-supplied," a syndicate manager involved in the transaction said.
"Especially in Japan and Asia there is a lot of concern that the market is too high, so buying from there is slow," he said.
The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note has tightened around 15 b.p. in the past week to just under 6.3 percent. A month ago the yield was 6.65 percent.
Similarly, five-year U.S. Treasury yields were around 10 b.p. lower than a week ago, at just under 6.2 percent. A month ago the yield was 6.5 percent.
The dollar has also strengthened during that time. This week it has been testing the 1.80 marks level, from around 1.76 marks a week ago and 1.73 a month ago.
The market's opinion was that the Kellogg bond was very aggressively priced. But an official at joint lead manager Lehman Brothers said it had received a "wonderful reaction".
He said bonds had been placed with Swiss, Middle Eastern and British investors.
"Spreads are under pressure in the 10-year dollar sector but the bid at around five years is still very strong," the official said.
The mark sector also saw further supply.
Allianz International Finance, guaranteed by German insurance company Allianz AG, launched a 1.5 billion mark 10-year bond, to be priced at 15 b.p. over Bunds.
An official at lead manager Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said the unrated firm was regarded as a triple-A credit by both domestic and international investors.
